content: 1. Moxifloxacin and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 2. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of itraconazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 3. Itraconazole increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 4. Co-administration of itraconazole with naloxegol is contraindicated as itraconazole significantly increases naloxegol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially causing opioid withdrawal symptoms. 5. Nefazodone increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transporters. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 6. Itraconazole increases nefazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor closely if co-administration is necessary. 7. Itraconazole increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transporters. The clinical significance is minor but should be monitored. 8. Itraconazole increases neratinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, and consider alternative therapies. 9. Itraconazole increases netupitant/palonosetron levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely, but no dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 10. Itraconazole increases nilotinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or reduce nilotinib dosage if unavoidable. 11. Itraconazole increases nimodipine levels and may enhance its negative inotropic effects. Monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction of concomitant drugs. 12. Itraconazole increases nintedanib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely for adverse effects, including dose reduction or discontinuation if necessary. 13. Nirmatrelvir increases itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Limit itraconazole dosage to 200 mg/day and monitor closely. 14. Itraconazole increases nisoldipine levels and may enhance its negative inotropic effects. Co-administration is contraindicated during and two weeks after itraconazole treatment. 15. Itraconazole increases nitrenedipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Nizatidine reduces itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 17. Itraconazole increases norgestrel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Itraconazole and nortriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 19. Itraconazole and octreotide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Itraconazole and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 21. Itraconazole and olanzapine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as rare cases of significant QTc prolongation have been reported with olanzapine. 22. Itraconazole increases olaparib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose and monitor closely. 23. Itraconazole increases oliceridine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate doses accordingly. 24. Itraconazole increases omaveloxolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose and monitor closely for adverse effects. 25. Itraconazole increases ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 26. Omeprazole reduces itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 27. Itraconazole increases ondansetron levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely, but no dosage adjustment is recommended. 28. Itraconazole and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with itraconazole and monitor closely. 29. Itraconazole increases osimertinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 30. Itraconazole increases ospemifene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Itraconazole and oxaliplatin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 32. Oxcarbazepine reduces itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is minor but should be monitored. 33. Itraconazole increases oxybutynin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Itraconazole increases oxycodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose reduction of oxycodone may be warranted when co-administered with itraconazole. 35. Itraconazole and ozanimod both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 36. Itraconazole increases paclitaxel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Itraconazole increases pacritinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 38. Itraconazole increases palbociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the palbociclib dose if unavoidable. 39. Itraconazole increases paliperidone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 40. Itraconazole increases palovarotene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 41. Itraconazole increases panobinostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 42. Itraconazole increases pantoprazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Administer proton pump inhibitors at least two hours before or after itraconazole. 43. Pantoprazole reduces itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 44. Itraconazole increases parecoxib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Itraconazole increases paricalcitol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Itraconazole and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 47. Itraconazole and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Itraconazole and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapies, and reduce the pazopanib dose if co-administration is unavoidable. 49. Itraconazole increases pemigatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative therapies, and adjust the pemigatinib dose if co-administration is unavoidable. 50. Itraconazole and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 51. Pentobarbital reduces itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 induction and inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. The clinical significance is minor but should be monitored.
